header.running_head: The Smiling and Laughing of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Haarith bin Jaz (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone smile as much as Rasulullaah ﷺ." In another narration, he says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ never laughed but only smiled."[^2]

Hadhrat Simaak bin Harb reports that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA), "Were you frequently in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ?" Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) replied, "Yes, I was often in his company. He never stood up from his place of performing the Fajr salaah until the sun rose. He would then get up while the Sahabah (RA) were sometimes discussing events that occurred during the Period of Ignorance. As they laughed, Rasulullaah ﷺ would merely smile."[^3]

In another narration, Hadhrat Simaak bin Harb reports that he once asked Hadhrat Jaabir bin Samurah (RA), "Were you frequently in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ?" Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) replied, "Yes. He often remained silent and would laugh very little. The Sahabah (RA) would often recite poetry to him and when he said something that made them laugh, he would merely smile."[^4]

Hadhrat Husayn bin Yazeed Kalbi (RA) says, "I have never seen Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh. He would only smile. There were also times when he would have to tie a rock to his belly because of extreme hunger."[^5]
Hadhrat Amrah questions Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) about Rasulullaah ﷺ's Domestic Life

Hadhrat Amrah reports that she once asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) about Rasulullaah ﷺ's behaviour when he was alone with his wives. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "He was like any other man except for the fact that he was the noblest of them all and the most compassionate. He also laughed and smiled very often."[^6]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "When revelation would come to Rasulullaah ﷺ or when he was delivering a lecture, he would appear like a person warning his people of an approaching punishment. However, when this was not happening, you would see that he had the most smiley face, was the most jovial of people and the handsomest of all men."[^7]
